C/C++ rows: nginx 1.31.4 with a custom C handler module built --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG' (debian:trixie); h2o pinned commit ccea64b, clang CMake Release -march=native -mtune=native, no LTO; mongoose 7.23 gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto; libreactorng pinned 7a65f8b and its server gcc -O3 -march=native; agensio v0.1.0-alpha.23 CMake Release -DAGENSIO_NATIVE=ON; proxygen CMake Release on the pinned facebook/proxygen base image with mimalloc; Drogon CMake Release (handler only) on the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image; userver v3.2 image, CMake Release -march=native; hical gcc-14 CMake Release -march=native -mtune=native (MDA2AV/HttpArena frameworks/<name>/Dockerfile).

The server container runs with seccomp=unconfined on the cpuset 0-31,64-95 for the H/1.1 profiles and the load generator on CPUs 32-63,96-127 of the same machine over loopback (scripts/lib/framework.sh, scripts/lib/profiles.sh, scripts/lib/common.sh). current.json is undated and describes the machine now, not necessarily at the date of each results file.
corrections.caveats: Mixed result: wins over nginx on the h2/h2c, TLS-JSON and pipelined profiles, but h2o and agensio are clearly ahead on h2 and h2c, the plain HTTP/1.1 baseline-4096 is 0.94x nginx and below h2o, mongoose, libreactorng, libioma and agensio, limited-conn-4096 is 0.88x nginx (2,301,647 vs 2,626,297), and static-h2-1024 is 0.25x nginx. The json-comp win is not Zig's: the entry's build.zig switches nilo's gzip to libdeflate, a C library (ADR 248), while the C++ rows compress with their own stacks; nginx, h2o and agensio do not run json-comp, so that profile compares only against the C++ frameworks userver, Drogon, hical and proxygen. TLS, by contrast, is tls.zig (pure Zig AES-GCM, needs the +aes+pclmul CPU flags). The README's '#2 of 79' is the framework board among untuned entries (nilo is type 'experimental'); nginx, h2o and agensio are 'infrastructure' and mongoose, libreactorng, libioma and proxygen are 'engine' entries, ranked on separate boards. The README's 1,401,412 req/s on four cores comes from nilo's own docs/comparison.md harness (Ryzen 7 9700X), which compares only Zig, Rust, Go, Node and Bun servers, no C/C++. Each HttpArena number is the best of 3 runs of 5 s (scripts/lib/common.sh RUNS=3, scripts/benchmark.sh), and rows come from different runs on the same machine: nilo.json was last written 2026-10-11 (PR #1539 by the nilo author), nginx.json and h2o.json 2026-08-30, drogon.json 2026-09-06, userver.json 2026-09-11 (git history). The nilo entry is maintained by the nilo author (meta.json maintainers: nevindra). The C competitor entries (nginx with a custom C handler module, libreactorng, libioma, h2o, mongoose) are minimal hand-written handlers built by the suite maintainers or contributors; the Drogon entry builds only its handler against the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image, so the Drogon ratios are weaker evidence than the nginx and h2o ratios. Bytes per response differ (derived from page data, bandwidth divided by req/s at baseline-4096): nilo, h2o, cpeak and kestrel 98.2, nginx 135.4, Drogon 134.4, libreactorng 108.7, libioma 85.8, mongoose 72.5. Pipelined (16x batched) and async-db are reference-only in HttpArena's framework composite score (site/content/docs/scoring/composite-score.md). 7 stars, released v0.8.0.
corrections.why_faster: Server architecture, not the language: fibers on zio with an io_uring backend (the containers run seccomp=unconfined, so io_uring is available), one allocation per request and about 4.7 KB per idle connection (nilo README, meta.json); the h2/h2c wins over nginx reflect nginx's slower HTTP/2 path in this suite (h2o is 2.2x ahead of nilo on h2, agensio 2.0x on h2 and 1.7x on h2c, derived from page data), and the json-comp win rests on libdeflate (C).

notes: All quoted numbers and ratios verified against the HttpArena JSON files; tier A kept on the HttpArena precedent. Corrected: runs are best of 3, not one; bytes per response for nilo is 98.2, not 62.9; same_algorithm set false because json-comp gzip is libdeflate (C) and the stacks differ. Shortcomings to record: behind nginx on baseline, limited-conn and static-h2, behind h2o and agensio on h2/h2c, json-comp win is libdeflate and only against C++ frameworks, pipelined reference-only, cross-run rows (nilo 2026-10-11 vs nginx 2026-08-30), entry maintained by the nilo author, 7 stars.

corrections.caveats: Weak claim. Kestrel is far behind the C and C++ servers on the main HTTP/1.1 profile: baseline-4096 1,320,795 is 0.40x nginx and 0.65x Drogon, limited-conn-4096 455,508 is 0.17x nginx, baseline-h2-256 2,360,754 is 0.69x nginx (h2o 16.1M), and baseline-h3-64 668,997 is 0.14x nginx (4.85M). The pipelined win over nginx is mostly nginx's pipelining cost, Kestrel loses pipelined to Drogon and Cutelyst, and pipelined is reference-only in HttpArena's framework and engine scoring. json-comp: nginx and h2o do not run it, so it compares only against the C++ frameworks; the entry answers brotli at quality 1 when the client offers br (gzip CompressionLevel.Fastest otherwise) and its responses average 1,582 bytes against 1,320 to 1,393 for the other rows (derived from page data), so the encoders and output differ; .NET's BrotliEncoder and GZipStream run native C brotli and zlib code. The frameworks/kestrel/README.md claim that JSON is serialized once at startup is stale: Dataset.cs serializes per request and says it keeps no precomputed responses. Kestrel is entered as type 'engine', so it is ranked on the engine board, not against the C++ frameworks. The entry is maintained by the suite owner (MDA2AV), not the ASP.NET team. Each number is the best of 3 runs of 5 s; rows come from different runs on the same machine (kestrel.json 2026-09-05, nginx.json and h2o.json 2026-08-30, drogon.json 2026-09-06, userver.json 2026-09-11 per git history). The TechEmpower plaintext tie is a 10 GbE-limited top group (ranks 1 to 13 within 0.8%, libreactor (C) rank 11 at 6,971,119), so it shows parity, not a win; that ranking is read from a screenshot in panjf2000/illustrations (benchmark/techempower-plaintext-top50-light.jpg), not the live results page. Every HttpArena entry is a minimal hand-written handler for the same endpoint contract (nginx runs a custom C handler module); Drogon is built against the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image.
corrections.why_faster: Not a language effect: Kestrel's pipelined lead over nginx is nginx's per-request pipelining cost (Drogon and Cutelyst beat Kestrel there), and its json-comp lead over userver, hical and Drogon comes with brotli quality 1 in native C code under .NET's System.IO.Compression and per-thread scratch buffers.

corrections.caveats: The README's '#1 of 95' (rust/README.md; the root README says '#1') is the HttpArena framework board filtered to flagship and emerging types with tuned entries shown (badge link type=emerging,flagship&tuned=1). nginx, h2o and agensio are 'infrastructure' and mongoose, libreactorng, libioma and proxygen are 'engine' entries, ranked on separate boards, and hical is 'experimental' (hidden by default), so the '#1' beats only the C++ frameworks Drogon, Cutelyst and userver. In the raw rows cpeak is 0.79x nginx at baseline-4096 and 0.81x at limited-conn-4096 (2,118,981 vs 2,626,297), and behind h2o, mongoose, agensio, libreactorng, libioma and hical (3,228,043) at baseline-4096. cpeak's meta.json declares mode 'tuned' (non-default configuration in HttpArena's terms) while the C++ framework entries are 'standard', though the entry README says default configuration. Pipelined and async-db are reference-only in the framework composite; the pipelined ratio vs nginx is mostly nginx's pipelining cost. TLS is rustls on ring, whose AES-GCM is BoringSSL-derived assembly. The cpeak entry was added 2026-10-11 by the cpeak author (meta.json maintainers: agile8118), and the README numbers were added the same day (commit c8fb314); rows come from different runs on the same machine (cpeak.json 2026-10-11, nginx.json and h2o.json 2026-08-30, drogon.json 2026-09-06, userver.json 2026-09-11 per git history). Each number is the best of 3 runs of 5 s. Every entry is a minimal hand-written handler for the same endpoint contract (nginx runs a custom C handler module), baseline-4096 mixes GET and POST with query parsing, and Drogon is built against the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image. The http-arena.com board itself could not be opened here (DNS failure), so the rank is taken from the README.
corrections.why_faster: Server architecture and libraries, not the language: hyper with one single-threaded Tokio event loop per core and SO_REUSEPORT listeners (no work stealing), mimalloc, sonic-rs JSON (SIMD) and per-request gzip/brotli (HttpArena entry README and meta.json); the C++ frameworks it beats (Drogon, Cutelyst, userver) are heavier stacks, while the C engines and nginx stay ahead.
